// divguard:path internal/codingagent/interactive.go

package codingagent

type InteractiveMode struct{ uiTaskCh chan func() }

// postUITask reproduces TUI-03: a full queue silently drops the task.
func (m *InteractiveMode) postUITask(fn func()) bool {
	select {
	case m.uiTaskCh <- fn: // want
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

type conn struct{ outCh chan []byte }

// send reproduces EXT-17: a full outbound queue drops the frame.
func (c *conn) send(data []byte) {
	select {
	case c.outCh <- data: // want
	default:
	}
}

// forward reproduces CDG-002: a capacity-1 queue fed from a loop keeps the
// first event and drops every later one.
func forward(events []int) chan int {
	out := make(chan int, 1)
	for _, ev := range events {
		select {
		case out <- ev: // want
		default:
		}
	}
	return out
}

// subscribe drops every callback value after the first.
func subscribe(register func(func(int))) chan int {
	updates := make(chan int, 1)
	register(func(v int) {
		select {
		case updates <- v: // want
		default:
		}
	})
	return updates
}

// rebound reuses the name for a second queue, so the send is not one-shot.
func rebound(v int) chan int {
	ch := make(chan int, 1)
	ch = make(chan int, 1)
	select {
	case ch <- v: // want
	default:
	}
	return ch
}

// sendTwice has one binding but two send sites; once the first send fills the
// channel, the second select drops its value.
func sendTwice(first, second int) chan int {
	ch := make(chan int, 1)
	select {
	case ch <- first: // want
	default:
	}
	select {
	case ch <- second: // want
	default:
	}
	return ch
}

// sendAfterPrefill includes the ordinary send when proving that the select is
// one-shot.
func sendAfterPrefill(first, second int) chan int {
	ch := make(chan int, 1)
	ch <- first
	select {
	case ch <- second: // want
	default:
	}
	return ch
}

// sendAfterAliasPrefill cannot prove a one-shot channel after it escapes
// through an alias.
func sendAfterAliasPrefill(first, second int) chan int {
	ch := make(chan int, 1)
	alias := ch
	alias <- first
	select {
	case ch <- second: // want
	default:
	}
	return ch
}

// sendAfterClosureLeak cannot prove a one-shot channel after a nested closure
// returns it to code that can prefill it.
func sendAfterClosureLeak(first, second int) chan int {
	ch := make(chan int, 1)
	leak := func() chan int { return ch }
	leak() <- first
	select {
	case ch <- second: // want
	default:
	}
	return ch
}
